ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, signatories and ultimate beneficiaries against the RMI FIU designated lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN list, UK HMT sanctions, and the RMI domestic list of persons engaged in serious crimes, pursuant to the RMI Anti-Money Laundering Regulations 2012 and FIU Guidance Notes. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by political exposure (PEP status), unexplained wealth, refusal to disclose UBO beyond the 25% threshold, and transactions involving high-risk money-laundering or terrorist-financing jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (all name submissions are made through licensed registered agents; public search interface: https://rmicorporate.org and official RMI e-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use the Latin alphabet; Marshallese and English proper words are acceptable. A non-Latin or foreign-language name must be transliterated into Latin characters and must be phonetically distinctive from existing RMI registered names. A certified transliteration certificate must accompany the name reservation for legal identity purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed corporate name, the applicant through its licensed registered agent may file a written Notice of Reconsideration with the Registrar within fifteen (15) business days of rejection, enclosing a legal memorandum and two alternative names. If the Registrar sustains the rejection on reconsideration, the applicant may file a petition for judicial review with the High Court of the Marshall Islands under Order 8 of the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, within thirty (30) days of the reconsideration decision, with representation by an RMI-admitted attorney being mandatory. The High Court may order the Registrar to accept a revised name upon a showing of lawful distinction and absence of public-policy harm.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for the operational headquarters and business functions, but the RMI Business Corporation must maintain a real physical registered office at the licensed registered agent's address in the Marshall Islands. For the proposed industry (cloud DevOps tools, database and API monitoring), no local RMI presence or physical operational premises are required; the statutory registered office may be the management address of the registered agent only.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The likelihood of unannounced physical on-site inspection is low, approximately 2% per annum, for a non-resident low-risk software infrastructure company with no local physical operations and no trigger events. If an FIU risk warning, sanctions alert, suspicious transaction report, or PEP involvement arises, inspection likelihood may rise to 15% or more within the following year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, 1990, as amended (Title 51, Marshall Islands Revised Code), Sections 23, 34, 45, 47, and 59
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (filed under Section 23 of the Business Corporations Act)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow deposit is required. Shares may be issued for such lawful consideration as fixed by the board of directors, including nominal or no-par value shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation adopts and ratifies the Articles of Incorporation as filed with the Registrar of Corporations; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscription for the initial common shares and declares the consideration received, if any, to be adequate; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation shall be maintained by the appointed Registered Agent in the Republic of the Marshall Islands; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and file permits; FURTHER RESOLVED, that actions taken by the incorporators and counsel to complete formation are hereby ratified. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations (RMI e-Registry portal or physical counter, Majuro)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the proposed corporate name. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered entities and must comply with RMI corporate suffix requirements. Pay the applicable reservation fee and obtain the reservation certificate, which is valid for 20 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or deemed confusingly similar, file an alternative name or submit a written request for reconsideration within 15 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public authorized to act for the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation including corporate name, initial registered agent and registered office, authorized share structure, permitted business purpose, and incorporator details. The incorporator must sign the articles before a notary public and the notarial certificate attached.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is defective, re-execute the signature and notarial certificate without altering substantive provisions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles with the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original notarized Articles of Incorporation, the Registered Agent Consent, and the official state filing fee of USD 275. Use standard processing unless expedited service is required. Keep a file-stamped copy for corporate records.
required_dossiers: Filing fee payment in the form of certified check, wire transfer, or online payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency or query, respond in writing within 30 days, provide any requested clarification, and pay any additional correction fee. A revised Articles document may be submitted if the query requires an amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Post-Formation Corporate Housekeeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The board then adopts Bylaws, issues share certificates to the initial subscribers, and records the minutes of the first board meeting and initial board resolutions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any share issuance or bylaw provision is defective, the board may ratify corrective resolutions retroactively, subject to shareholder approval if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Designation and Maintenance of Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations and licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain a licensed RMI registered agent with a physical street address in the Marshall Islands. The registered office is the registered agent's street address. Any change of registered agent or office must be filed with the Registrar using the prescribed change form.
required_dossiers: Registered Agent and Registered Office confirmation
Change of Registered Agent form (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or is disqualified, appoint a successor agent within 30 days and file the change notice with the Registrar to avoid administrative dissolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Banking / Compliance Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations and financial institution onboarding officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Order a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar to verify legal existence for banking or corporate account purposes. Prepare the corporate kit, beneficial ownership registers, and board resolutions required by banks, including Mercury or Stripe onboarding due diligence.
required_dossiers: Register of shareholders / beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the Certificate of Good Standing, cure any outstanding annual franchise tax or filing default, then re-apply. If a bank queries corporate authority, supply a board resolution confirming officer signing authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing licensing board is required for ISIC 6201 developer infrastructure and cloud services in the Marshall Islands.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — a general RMI business license is only needed if the corporation establishes physical operations with local source revenue; a non-resident cloud business is exempt.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — software/cloud operations involve no physical installation, point-source discharge, or hazardous material handling.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial discharge and zero VOC emissions from cloud infrastructure. If any office space is physically occupied, comply with RMI-EPA solid waste and used-electronics disposal provisions, and maintain no on-site wastewater discharge beyond standard municipal connection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If a physical office is established, obtain a fire safety certificate from the Marshall Islands Fire Department for the occupied premises, verify general structural load capacity only for standard office equipment, and implement basic occupational safety and health measures (electrical safety, egress, and first-aid) in accordance with RMI workplace safety standards. For a purely non-resident cloud operation, such clearances are not triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance, Office of Revenue and Taxation, operating as Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs (MIRC), which administers customs duties, excise, and all revenue statutes through the ASYCUDA World electronic single-window portal; corporate registration is separately administered by the Registrar of Corporations under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; employment-linked contributions are administered by the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration (MISSA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned, non-resident Business Corporation (BC) incorporated under the Business Corporations Act 1990 (BCCA, 27 MIRC Ch. 4) has no inshore taxable nexus and is statutorily exempt from all national income, capital gains, withholding, franchise, and indirect taxes. Step 1: File Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation; no national TIN is issued for income tax because no income tax exists. Step 2 (conditional): if importing physical goods, register for a Customs Client Code in ASYCUDA World before the first declaration. Step 3 (conditional): if hiring employees physically located in the RMI, register as an employer with MISSA and obtain an employer contribution number. Step 4 (conditional): if maintaining an office or staff in an urban local-government area, procure a municipal business license (e.g., Majuro Atoll Local Government). Step 5 (banking evidence): request a Certificate of Tax Exemption / Tax Status Letter from the Ministry of Finance confirming BCCA Section 107 exemption, for presentation to Stripe Billing, Mercury, and correspondent banks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, hybrid-mismatch, pass-through election, or entity-level taxation election exists in RMI domestic law; the Section 107 BCCA exemption is automatic, perpetual, and non-elective for a foreign-owned non-resident BC. The RMI has not enacted BEPS Action 2 hybrid-mismatch rules and offers no OECD-style classification election. A BC may voluntarily assume contractual tax payments or make ex-gratia payments to the RMI Government, but this is a private contractual undertaking rather than a statutory election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Import customs duty system under the Customs Act 1990 (27 MIRC Ch. 1), as amended; the Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no VAT, GST, or general sales-and-use tax and is not a member of any customs union.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 0. No turnover-based indirect-tax threshold exists because no VAT/GST is levied. A Customs Client Code registration obligation arises at the first importation of commercial goods into the RMI, irrespective of value. Offshore export of DevOps tools, database monitoring, and API infrastructure services to foreign customers triggers no RMI indirect-tax registration. Municipal business license registration is triggered only by physical business presence within a local-government jurisdiction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate exists. Within the customs environment, however, all import and export declarations must be filed electronically in MIRC's ASYCUDA World system, which generates a customs electronic assessment and cargo control number before goods release. No API-based fiscal clearance applies to Stripe Billing issuance of invoices or Mercury ACH payment flows; no fiscal value is required on commercial invoices for offshore software subscription services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable as a VAT refund or input-credit mechanism because the RMI levies no VAT/GST on exports or on cross-border digital services. SaaS DevOps tools, database monitoring, and API monitoring infrastructure services exported to foreign customers fall outside the territorial scope of RMI taxation and generate no indirect-tax liability. For exports of physical goods from RMI territory, customs duty is not assessed where the exporter files a valid export declaration and complies with the Customs Act and the Shipping Act (27 MIRC Ch. 5); there is no export-refund pool, no carry-forward credit, and no withholding-recovery mechanism to substantiate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ASYCUDA World electronic customs export declaration (E-Declaration form, CUS-EX)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (house and master copies, as applicable)
Commercial invoice and packing list reflecting HS tariff classification, value, quantity, and consignee
Inward remittance certificate or bank SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of foreign sale proceeds
Certificate of Origin or Certificate of Non-Manufacture where preferential tariff or transshipment treatment is claimed
RMI vessel or aircraft license data and cargo manifest when the export moves on an RMI-flagged carrier
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Since no VAT exists, zero-rating fraud and VAT clawback cannot arise; MIRC audit scrutiny focuses on customs under-valuation, tariff mis-description, forged export declarations, and unlicensed trading. Under the Customs Act, a false or materially misleading export/import declaration subjects the goods to seizure and forfeiture, retrospective recovery of duty up to 100% of the evaded amount, pecuniary penalties, and imprisonment for fraudulent declarants. False BCCA filings or misrepresentations concerning non-resident tax-exempt status may result in administrative dissolution, reinstatement penalties, and civil liability before the High Court. Falsification of remittance documentation is additionally prosecutable under the RMI Criminal Code, with asset-forfeiture remedies. All supporting export documentation must be retained for at least five years and produced to MIRC within 14 days of a written demand.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), acting as prudential regulator under the Banking Act 1995 (as amended); the U.S. Federal Reserve System serves as the de facto monetary authority because the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender; the RMI has been an IMF member since 1992 and has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMI has no domestic currency, no indigenous central bank, no exchange control statute, and no foreign-investment screening regime. The U.S. dollar is legal tender; current-account and capital-account transactions are fully and freely convertible and transferable without RMI approval. Profit, dividend, and liquidation remittances by a non-resident Business Corporation are entirely unrestricted and carry no RMI withholding tax, capital gains tax, or remittance quota. For ISIC 6201 developer-infrastructure, database, and API-monitoring cloud services, the business model is treated as tax-exempt international business. Practical frictions arise only from U.S. correspondent-bank OFAC screening, documentary CDD, and fintech account eligibility policies; no frictions arise from RMI currency convertibility. The absence of an onshore FX market means all hedging and conversion activity occurs offshore in U.S. or international banking centers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. The RMI imposes no statutory surrender, forced conversion, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio on export receipts or service revenues. MH_BC may retain 100% of its USD cloud-subscription proceeds in a U.S. fintech settlement account or an RMI-licensed bank without conversion into any local currency. The only compliance duties are ordinary tax-information reporting (for U.S.-source revenue streams collected through Stripe Billing), accurate sub-ledger recordkeeping available to the RMI registered agent, and adherence to the target payment rails' settlement terms. No RMI form, filing, or license is required to hold or disburse export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Current Account plus segregated Capital Escrow sub-account for subscribed share capital and infrastructure reserve

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam - Republic of the Marshall Islands Branch, Majuro

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Developmental credit facility only - not suitable for treasury liquidity, escrow, or trade clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for the designated treasury rails. Mercury is the recommended primary operating account provider for MH_BC: it is a U.S. fintech operating with FDIC-insured partner banks, offers native USD ACH and Fedwire clearing, fully remote onboarding, and practical acceptance of an RMI non-resident Business Corporation holding a U.S. EIN. Stripe Billing functions as the collection-side rail only and requires the Mercury or other settlement account for payout. Legal constraints: (i) the RMI Banking Act 1995 does not regulate foreign fintechs or EMIs that are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in the RMI, so no RMI banking license is triggered by using Mercury or Stripe; (ii) the U.S. corporate transparency beneficial-ownership reporting obligation applies if the entity registers to do business in any U.S. state, and the U.S. FinCEN expectation of a BOI report must be assessed; (iii) the fintechs own counterparty risk policy governs acceptance; (iv) FATCA/Form W-8BEN-E documentation is required for U.S. withholding; (v) independent EMIs such as Wise Business are rated Medium viability as supplementary FX conversion and low-value payout channels but should not be the sole clearing account because they lack a native U.S. ABA-routed corporate checking capability comparable to Mercury. No RMI-licensed digital EMI of competitive scale currently exists for USD clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted and operationally recommended for MH_BC through Mercury and Stripe Billing: no director physical appearance is required, provided each 25% or greater beneficial owner completes liveness or video identity verification with a passport or government-issued ID and the corporate record set is submitted in certified form. For RMI domestic banks (BMI and Bank of Guam RMI Branch), the practical KYC mandate is stricter: physical in-branch attendance is generally expected, or alternatively an original notarized and apostilled power of attorney designating an RMI-resident signatory, a current certificate of good standing, registered-agent confirmation, board resolution, and UBO documentation. There is no RMI statute requiring physical board attendance for account opening; the mandate is policy-based at the bank level. Therefore MH_BC can complete the entire Stage 4 treasury build without traveling to Majuro if the Mercury/Stripe blueprint is adopted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident offshore-incorporated Business Corporation with no local payroll, no RMI office, and a government-defined Tax_Exempt_Zone classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registrar-issued Certificate of Good Standing dated within 30 days, certified Memorandum and Articles of Association under the Nonresident Business Corporations Act, RMI registered-agent consent letter, board resolution establishing the bank mandate and signatory authority, UBO declaration with passports and residential address proof for all 25% or greater owners, corporate group structure chart, and an ISIC 6201 business plan documenting the DevOps cloud infrastructure, database, and API monitoring commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity Stripe Billing subscription receivables arriving into a newly opened treasury account without a matching revenue trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed customer SaaS or API-monitoring terms of service and subscription agreements, 6-to-12-month Stripe payout ledger exported and mapped to the general ledger, invoicing system output and merchant-of-record evidence, redacted client roster, live product dashboard URL, and daily reconciliation tickets linking each Mercury ACH settlement batch to the subscription sub-ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection disproportionate to the stated cloud-infrastructure business, lacking source-of-funds documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notice and board resolution authorizing the equity injection, source-of-funds records from the contributing shareholder (bank statements, dividend or liquidation distribution schedules, salary or investment gain evidence), designation of the Capital Escrow sub-account, funds-flow projection for the ISIC 6201 infrastructure build-out, and written legal confirmation that the injected funds originate from legitimate taxed or exempt sources and not from foreign tax evasion, corruption, or sanctioned jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent-bank adverse perception of an RMI-incorporated offshore entity under industry-wide de-risking patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of FATF and Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering participation with no current FATF high-risk designation, RMI Financial Intelligence Unit registration status under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2000, banking risk-tier confirmation that ISIC 6201 requires no statutory license and is classified Low_Risk_Standard, an AML/CFT policy manual, directors-and-officers and cyber liability insurance certificates, and if available a banking reference letter from the ultimate shareholder's existing institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections must be routed as USD same-day Fedwire (domestic) or SWIFT MT103 (cross-border) directly to the designated Capital Escrow Account at Mercury, using the routing and account number certified in the Mercury onboarding package. The SWIFT Field 70 remittance information must state: CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION MH_BC PER BOARD RESOLUTION, and the ordering customer name must exactly match the contributing shareholder named in the capital call. For U.S.-originating contributions, use Fedwire with payment descriptor EQUITY CAPITAL INJECTION and avoid ACH IAT because the ordering bank is outside the U.S. Prior to transfer, complete the treasury pre-notification CDD ticket attaching the capital call notice, board resolution, source-of-funds statements, and escrow designation memo; upon receipt, reconcile the incoming cover or MT103 payment confirmation within T+1 against the treasury ledger. Stripe Billing must never be used for capital injections, and the account mandate should prohibit crypto, gambling, or personal-consumption references. A U.S. EIN is required before the account is opened, and all wire instructions should be verified telephonically or by bank-approved two-channel confirmation to prevent payment diversion fraud.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement for MH_BC uses a tiered clearing architecture: (i) SWIFT MT103 for international vendor payments (cloud infrastructure, database software, API bandwidth, colocation providers), citing the underlying ISIC 6201 service contract and displaying invoice or purchase order numbers in Field 70, with correspondent charge instruction SHA to avoid beneficiary shortfall; (ii) Mercury ACH CCD or SEC for domestic U.S. vendor disbursements and operating costs; (iii) Fedwire for same-day strategic payments where vendor terms require collection by value date; and (iv) commercial letters of credit (documentary L/C) reserved for high-value hardware, server, or network equipment procurement where the vendor demands bank payment undertaking - although an L/C is not operationally efficient for recurring SaaS or DevOps charges. Stripe Billing manages the collection side, netting merchant processing fees before settling to the Mercury account; treasury should run a daily bank-sub-ledger reconciliation, sweep excess operational cash into the capital reserve balance band, and maintain an approved vendor payment matrix with dual-signatory approval above USD 25,000 per transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, JPY/USD) executed with U.S. or international bank counterparties under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or an FX Global Code-adherent master agreement, used to hedge non-USD software subscription revenue streams without involvement of any RMI-regulated exchange.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible for currencies lacking deliverable USD liquidity (e.g., CNY, KRW, INR) because no RMI central-bank restriction applies to offshore NDF contracting; such contracts require an ISDA credit support annex and must be cash-settled in USD at maturity.

Cross-currency swaps (USD versus EUR or GBP) for multi-year committed-use infrastructure contracts, included under a cross-currency interest-rate swap line with a U.S. international bank; the RMI has no derivatives licensing statute or mandatory clearing location, and execution is conditioned on a board-approved hedging policy and, where relevant, the U.S. CFTC end-user exception for commercial treasury risk.

OTC foreign-exchange options (plain vanilla calls and puts) on the same currency pairs for downside protection on material undisbursed subscription balances, permitted only where the counterparty bank credit limit has been approved by the board and the option premium is expensed against treasury cost.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Annual Franchise-Tax Renewal (Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Entities Division, Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the last day of the month in which the certificate of incorporation anniversary falls. Example: a corporation incorporated on 12 March must file and pay on or before 31 March each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late penalty after the anniversary deadline; additional accrual penalties may apply. Failure to file and pay for two consecutive annual periods gives the Registrar authority to administratively dissolve and strike the corporation; reinstatement requires payment of all arrears, penalties, current annual fee and the Registrar's reinstatement filing fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent; confidential register maintained at the RMI registered office and accessible to the RMI Registrar / financial intelligence authorities on lawful demand.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due together with the annual report and before the corporate renewal date; share transfers during the preceding year must be reflected in the UBO register within 14 days of each transfer, with final confirmation as of the annual renewal date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-delivery or false confirmation of UBO information may expose the company and directors to monetary penalties under RMI AML/CFT and beneficial-ownership regulations; continuing non-compliance may be treated as a ground for registered-agent resignation or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Continuity Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent / Registrar of Corporations, Business Entities Division, RMI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The RMI-registered agent must remain in office at all times; annual consent is collected with the annual report, and any change or resignation must be filed within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of registered agent or registered office for more than 30 days permits the Registrar to commence administrative dissolution; the corporation must appoint a new RMI licensed agent and pay all outstanding fees before a certificate of good standing can be issued.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is compulsory for a non-resident, non-public Business Corporation based solely on revenue, asset, or shareholder count. An audit is mandatory only if the corporation is admitted to a securities exchange, licensed as a bank, insurance/reinsurance company, trust company, or captive in the RMI, or if shareholders representing the prescribed voting threshold demand an independent audit under the Business Corporations Act. For this ISIC 6201 SaaS/DevOps holding company, no audit obligation exists unless imposed by a lender, investor, or customer contract.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: RMI has no local statutory GAAP. The board must elect either IFRS or US GAAP for internal financial statements; IFRS is the default framework for third-party/reporting purposes, and US GAAP is acceptable where the parent or investor reports under US GAAP. No financial statements are required to be filed annually with the RMI Registrar for a non-resident BC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a confidential beneficial-ownership register at the RMI registered office. Annually, before or with the annual report, the board or appointed corporate secretary must confirm to the registered agent that the register is complete, accurate, and current. Share transfers and any resulting change in ownership or voting control must be recorded in the Register of Members and in the beneficial-ownership register within 14 days of the transfer; the annual cycle therefore operates as a reconciliation of all shareholding movements. Non-resident direct or indirect shareholders are permitted. The UBO register is not filed on the public record but must be made available to the RMI Registrar or financial intelligence unit upon lawful request. Nominee shareholders or intermediary arrangements must be disclosed to the registered agent but are not publicly registered.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders' ledger with issued, transferred, and cancelled share details)
Register of Directors (identifying details, appointment dates, and cessation dates)
Minute Book (minutes and written consents of shareholder and director meetings)
Confidential Register of Beneficial Owners (maintained by the registered agent)
Register of Mortgages and Charges (if any security interests are created by the company)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$600 - US$1,200 per year; typical market rate for a non-resident Business Corporation with standard share capital and no physical RMI office is US$750 - US$1,000, including annual report preparation, UBO confirmation and secretarial support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000 - US$8,000 per engagement if a voluntary, shareholder-demanded, or lender-required audit of the DevOps/SaaS holding company is commissioned; not an annual statutory line item for an exempt non-resident BC.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) imposes no corporate income tax on a non-resident Business Corporation (a 'non-resident domestic corporation' under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, BCCA). No profits tax, capital gains tax, gross receipts tax, or branch remittance tax is levied on income derived from outside the RMI.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Total statutory tax exemption for non-resident domestic corporations under BCCA Section 107 (exemption from taxation). The RMI does not operate an income tax code; therefore no effective tax rate applies, no foreign tax credit mechanism exists, and no payroll or social tax is triggered by foreign-based staff. The only mandatory recurring impost is the Registry of Corporations annual report fee, which is a corporate registry charge, not a tax. Because no income tax base exists, carried-forward tax losses are not recognised (statutory carryforward limit: 0 years).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Not applicable — no RMI corporate income tax return exists. The sole mandatory recurring statutory filing for an MH Business Corporation is the BCCA Annual Report filed with the Registrar of Corporations through a licensed registered agent; the agent submits it via the RMI corporate registry electronic portal or on paper. No revenue authority filing, profit declaration, or audited financial statement is required by RMI law for a non-resident BC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, on the anniversary of the date of incorporation, not on a calendar fiscal-year basis.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Report must be filed on or before the thirtieth day following the anniversary date of the certificate of incorporation. The RMI fiscal year has no statutory role; the company may adopt any accounting period for internal and foreign-filing purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name of the MH Business Corporation as stated in the certificate of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the registered legal name only. A trade name or product brand (e.g., API monitoring product) has no filing effect; a DBA is not available or required for non-resident BCs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annual Report Item 2: Registered agent and registered office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and physical street address of the licensed registered agent in the RMI; the registered office must be in the RMI and open for service of process.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the agent's street address in Majuro or Ebeye; a post office box is insufficient. Non-resident status does not waive the registered agent requirement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annual Report Item 3: Authorized share capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of authorized shares, par value or no-par designation, and aggregate authorized capital; this determines the annual report fee tier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the capital structure exactly as in the articles of incorporation. No minimum capital is required; a typical non-resident BC uses 500,000 shares at USD 0.001 par value or no-par shares.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annual Report Item 4: Directors and officers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, residential addresses, and nationalities of all directors and officers, including alternates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident individuals and corporate directors are permitted. Foreign addresses are acceptable. Nominee directors must be disclosed to the registered agent for beneficial-ownership record-keeping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annual Report Item 5: Nature of business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Concise statement of the general business purpose of the corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an ISIC 6201 DevOps cloud-tools business, state: 'International software development, cloud infrastructure, database and API monitoring services.' Confirm that no business is conducted within the RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annual Report Item 6: Issued and outstanding shares
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of issued shares and total consideration received for those shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all issued shares, including uncertificated book-entry shares. The registered agent must maintain the share register and a register of transfers; non-resident holders require no RMI entry in the public register.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fees accrue from the 31st day after the anniversary date, scaled by authorized capital and period of delay. After notice and a further 30 days of default, the Registrar of Corporations revokes the certificate of incorporation; the corporation is struck from the register and loses legal capacity to contract or hold assets in its own name. Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable for debts and obligations incurred after revocation. Reinstatement is discretionary and requires payment of all arrears, late fees, and a reinstatement fee.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — the RMI imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by an MH Business Corporation. Dividends may be declared and paid in any currency, typically USD, without ministerial approval, subject to the BCCA solvency rule that the corporation must remain able to pay its debts as they fall due and that total assets must exceed total liabilities after the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI maintains no comprehensive double-taxation agreements; therefore treaty-based dividend, interest, or royalty relief cannot be invoked at RMI source. Tax relief is instead pursued in the shareholder's residence jurisdiction through CFC, PFIC, or foreign tax credit rules. To evidence non-resident tax status, a shareholder should obtain: (1) a Certificate of Good Standing and a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation from the RMI Registrar; (2) a letter from the licensed registered agent confirming non-resident domestic corporation status and zero RMI tax-filing history; (3) an annual report compliance certificate; and (4) for US payment processors, IRS Form W-8BEN-E to avoid US backup withholding. The RMI participates in the Global Forum and has committed to exchange of information; a tax residency certificate is not an RMI fiscal instrument because the RMI does not operate an income tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory RMI rates are 0% on arm's-length interest and 0% on royalties paid by an MH BC to non-resident lenders or licensors. There is no deemed-income recharacterization of excessive interest or royalties under RMI law; however, the BCCA board solvency and fiduciary rules restrict distributions that impair creditor claims. No DTA-reduced rates exist because the RMI has no comprehensive income tax treaty network.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable — the RMI has no transfer-pricing statute, no arm's-length codification, no Local File or Master File regime, and no contemporaneous documentation threshold. Transactions are conventionally maintained in USD, and any intercompany pricing defense must be prepared for the foreign tax authority of the ultimate parent (e.g., US, UK, or Singapore) rather than for RMI compliance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. The RMI Economic Substance (Amendment) Act 2021 and the Economic Substance Regulations 2021 require RMI-incorporated entities conducting a 'relevant activity' to file an annual Economic Substance Return and demonstrate adequate economic substance in the RMI. A developer-infrastructure, database, and API-monitoring cloud business (ISIC 6201) will typically be classified under 'Intellectual Property Business' where income is derived from licensing or exploitation of software code, algorithms, APIs, or databases, or under 'Distribution and Service Centre Business' where services are rendered to related parties. A non-resident BC with no RMI office, no RMI employees, and no board management in the RMI cannot satisfy the default substance test. The test is treated as satisfied, however, if the entity is tax resident and subject to full tax on its profits in a foreign jurisdiction and relies on the information-exchange route; otherwise the BC must demonstrate RMI premises, local employees, local operating expenditure, and core income-generating activities performed in the RMI. Non-compliance is reported to the OECD, attracts monetary penalties, and can lead to strike-off of the corporation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion in the Beneficial Owner's Home Jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A US, UK, or EU tax-resident beneficial owner uses the MH BC and its US payment rails (Stripe Billing, Mercury ACH) to divert SaaS and API-monitoring subscription revenue without declaring the income; the owner is the sole signatory, has no genuine board control, and no controlled-foreign-corporation filing (e.g., US Form 5471) or equivalent disclosure is made.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil fraud penalties of up to 75% of the tax underpayment in the US (IRC Section 6663) or corresponding EU/UK offshore penalties up to 200% of the tax; criminal tax evasion charges carrying imprisonment (up to 5 years per count in the US; up to 7 years in the UK); seizure of bank accounts at Mercury and Stripe-linked reserves through mutual legal assistance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The RMI corporate veil can be disregarded on sham or agency grounds, imposing joint and several personal liability on the controlling shareholder/director for the corporation's tax debts; foreign freezing orders and charging orders attach to the BC's assets; the director faces travel bans, arrest warrants, and extradition through Interpol Red Notices.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance Under RMI ESR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The BC operates as a letterbox entity with no RMI physical presence, no local director or secretary, no board meetings, and no Economic Substance Return; all functions are performed from a high-tax country, and the entity is not tax resident or fully taxed in any foreign jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to file the ESR return triggers a fixed penalty (commonly in the tens of thousands of USD) plus daily default penalties; providing false substance information attracts additional fines and director disqualification; the licensed registered agent must report the entity, and the Registrar may strike the corporation off the register, annulling its legal personality and contracts with cloud and banking providers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face disqualification orders in the RMI and personal fines for false declarations; foreign courts are likely to pierce the veil and treat the BC as a nullity, making the beneficial owner personally liable for all trading debts and triggering asset-freeze orders against the owner's personal accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Registry Default / Annual Report Omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the BCCA Annual Report and pay the registry fee for one or more successive anniversary cycles while continuing to invoice customers and hold funds through Stripe Billing and Mercury ACH accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar of Corporations revokes the certificate of incorporation and strikes the company from the RMI register; the corporation ceases to exist as a legal entity, contracts and subscription agreements become unenforceable in its name, and bank/payment-rail accounts are frozen or closed once the bank learns of dissolution; reinstatement requires full arrears, penalties, and a discretionary filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who act or contract on behalf of a dissolved corporation are, under BCCA-derived principles, jointly and severally personally liable for all obligations incurred after dissolution; the veil is pierced by operation of law; the controlling owner faces personal recovery suits from creditors and potential disqualification as a director for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership Concealment in Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealment of the ultimate beneficial owner through nominee shareholdings, bearer arrangements, or undisclosed trust structures when opening accounts at Mercury and Stripe Billing; routing software-subscription revenue through the BC without authentic operating substance; making repeated related-party transfers to high-risk or secrecy-haven accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI AML regulations require the registered agent to terminate the relationship and report suspicious activity to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit; US FinCEN penalties can reach USD 250,000 (or twice the transaction value) per violation for willful failures; money-laundering convictions in the US and EU carry imprisonment of up to 20 years; payment processors may terminate merchant accounts and place the funds in extended holds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and signatories who submit false beneficial-ownership declarations face fines, disqualification, and criminal prosecution; the beneficial owner can be extradited for wire fraud and money-laundering; cross-border freezing orders attach to both corporate and personal assets, and travel bans are routinely imposed pending extradition proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, management fees, or shareholder loans while the BC is insolvent or would be rendered insolvent; stripping cash out of the BC before creditor claims; making distributions without board approval or without satisfying the BCCA balance-sheet and liquidity tests; transferring assets at a significant undervalue to the beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Directors who consent to an unlawful distribution are jointly and severally liable to restore the corporation or compensate creditors; on insolvency, a liquidator can avoid transactions at an undervalue as fraudulent conveyances and claw back distributions for the statutory vulnerability period; foreign bankruptcy courts may recognize reciprocal RMI liquidation proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The beneficial owner as a shadow director is personally liable to restore the full amount of the unlawful distribution without limitation of liability; the corporate veil is pierced to recover traceable assets; fraudulent trading during insolvency can result in civil compensation, criminal sanctions, and personal travel restrictions pending enforcement of foreign judgment summonses.
